newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Maize, milling wheat futures down in Budapest.
newsitem.headline: Maize, milling wheat futures down in Budapest.

text.p: Maize and milling wheat futures ended mostly lower on the Budapest Commodity Exchange, dealers said on Tuesday.
The exception was the March maturity, where speculators sought to close positions.
March milling wheat ended at 25,300 forints per tonne and one dealer said prices were likely to peak around 26,000.
"That would be a level where producers might sell again," said Robert Monostori of Agrimpex.
He added that most of the 900 open contracts for March were likely to be actually delivered.
Sandor Ifju of OTP Forex said he expected March to remain steady or go slightly higher over the next few days as remaining speculative contracts were closed.
Most other milling wheat maturities fell by 170 to 300 forints, with the July maturity dropping most, to 19,600 from 19,900.
Scope was seen for further lossses in the July position as it remained above both August and September.
"This is an illiquid maturity and prone to sudden movements but it will eventually drop back to below August or September prices (of 19,100 and 19,260 respectively)."
March maize rose 50 forints to end at 17,750 but the upward pressure was not as strong as in milling wheat, Monostori said.
"There is hardly any upward drive in the market," he said.
July was the most actively traded maize position with almost half the day's maize turnover. It was also the one with the highest number of open contracts, and ended at 16,700 forints, down 200.
Total turnover was a below-average 621.58 million forints, or 1,551 contracts, of which 941 were for milling wheat and 459 for maize.
Lot size is 20,000 kg for all contracts.
